/-!
# Conjecture 4.74

by V. P. Shunkov

b) Is every binary-finite $2$-group of order greater than $2$ non-simple?

A group is *binary finite* if any two of its elements generate a finite
subgroup. A $2$-group is a group in which every element has order a power
of $2$; it may be infinite. A finite $2$-group of order greater than $2$ is
nilpotent and hence non-simple, so the content of the question lies in the
infinite case. Only part b) of Problem 4.74 appears in the notebook.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

blocks.code:
def IsBinaryFinite (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ x y : G, Finite (Subgroup.closure {x, y})
blocks.docstring:
A group $G$ is *binary finite* if any two elements $x, y \in G$ generate a
finite subgroup $\langle x, y \rangle$.

justification.closest_existing_considered: Mathlib has no locally-finite-group or n-generator-finiteness predicate; the closest are Monoid.IsTorsion (only 1-generated subgroups finite, strictly weaker) and Finite G (strictly stronger). Neither is faithful, so a new definition was required.
justification.name: Kourovka.«4.74».IsBinaryFinite
justification.why_needed: Shunkov's notion of a binary finite group (every subgroup generated by two elements is finite) does not exist in Mathlib or FormalConjecturesForMathlib. Defined as ∀ x y : G, Finite (Subgroup.closure {x, y}). Two small API lemmas are included (finite groups are binary finite; binary finite groups are torsion), following the repository's request for basic API tests of bespoke definitions.

@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsBinaryFinite.isTorsion {G : Type*} [Group G] (hG : IsBinaryFinite G) :
    Monoid.IsTorsion G := by
  intro x
  have hx : Finite (Subgroup.zpowers x) := by
    rw [Subgroup.zpowers_eq_closure, ← Set.pair_eq_singleton x]
    exact hG x x
  have h : IsOfFinOrder (⟨x, Subgroup.mem_zpowers x⟩ : Subgroup.zpowers x) :=
    isOfFinOrder_of_finite _
  rw [← orderOf_pos_iff, Subgroup.orderOf_mk, orderOf_pos_iff] at h
  exact h

theorem kourovka.«4.74».parts.b : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], IsPGroup 2 G → IsBinaryFinite G →
      (Infinite G ∨ 2 < Nat.card G) → ¬ IsSimpleGroup G := by

blocks.docstring:
b) Is every binary-finite $2$-group of order greater than $2$ non-simple?

The group $G$ is allowed to be infinite, so "order greater than $2$" is stated
as `Infinite G ∨ 2 < Nat.card G` (recall that `Nat.card G = 0` when `G` is
infinite). This hypothesis excludes exactly the trivial group and the group of
order $2$, the only simple $2$-groups of order at most $2$.

claims.decomposer_note: Yes/no question: for every group G that is a 2-group (IsPGroup 2 G) and binary finite (every subgroup generated by two elements is finite), and whose order exceeds 2 (which must include infinite G — Nat.card is 0 on infinite types, so encode as Infinite G ∨ 2 < Nat.card G — since finite 2-groups of order > 2 are nilpotent hence trivially non-simple, the real content is the infinite case), G is not simple (¬ IsSimpleGroup G); the order > 2 hypothesis exactly excludes the trivial group and ℤ/2, the only simple 2-groups of order ≤ 2; single lettered part b) of a multi-part problem, so slot keeps the letter.
claims.reviewer_why: All eight candidates state the identical proposition: answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], IsPGroup 2 G → (∀ x y, Finite (Subgroup.closure {x, y})) → (Infinite G ∨ 2 < Nat.card G) → ¬ IsSimpleGroup G. This is a faithful rendering: IsPGroup 2 is the elementwise 2-group notion valid for infinite groups; binary finiteness is Shunkov's 'any two elements generate a finite subgroup'; the order hypothesis is strict and includes infinite groups while excluding exactly the trivial group and Z/2; ¬ IsSimpleGroup is correct since nontriviality follows from the order hypothesis. c04 chosen for style: a named bespoke IsBinaryFinite definition (as CONTRIBUTING encourages) with two @[category API] sanity lemmas (finite ⇒ binary finite; binary finite ⇒ torsion), both with real proofs, and docstrings explaining the domain restriction. Only the module docstring was lightly edited. Compiles with only the 'declaration uses sorry' warning.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 4.74

by V. P. Shunkov

b) Is every binary-finite $2$-group of order greater than $2$ non-simple?

A group is *binary finite* if any two of its elements generate a finite
subgroup. A $2$-group is a group in which every element has order a power
of $2$; it may be infinite. A finite $2$-group of order greater than $2$ is
nilpotent and hence non-simple, so the content of the question lies in the
infinite case. Only part b) of Problem 4.74 appears in the notebook.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«4.74»

/-- A group $G$ is *binary finite* if any two elements $x, y \in G$ generate a
finite subgroup $\langle x, y \rangle$. -/
def IsBinaryFinite (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ x y : G, Finite (Subgroup.closure {x, y})

/-- Every finite group is binary finite. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsBinaryFinite.of_finite (G : Type*) [Group G] [Finite G] : IsBinaryFinite G :=
  fun _ _ => inferInstance

/-- Every element of a binary finite group has finite order. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsBinaryFinite.isTorsion {G : Type*} [Group G] (hG : IsBinaryFinite G) :
    Monoid.IsTorsion G := by
  intro x
  have hx : Finite (Subgroup.zpowers x) := by
    rw [Subgroup.zpowers_eq_closure, ← Set.pair_eq_singleton x]
    exact hG x x
  have h : IsOfFinOrder (⟨x, Subgroup.mem_zpowers x⟩ : Subgroup.zpowers x) :=
    isOfFinOrder_of_finite _
  rw [← orderOf_pos_iff, Subgroup.orderOf_mk, orderOf_pos_iff] at h
  exact h

/--
b) Is every binary-finite $2$-group of order greater than $2$ non-simple?

The group $G$ is allowed to be infinite, so "order greater than $2$" is stated
as `Infinite G ∨ 2 < Nat.card G` (recall that `Nat.card G = 0` when `G` is
infinite). This hypothesis excludes exactly the trivial group and the group of
order $2$, the only simple $2$-groups of order at most $2$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«4.74».parts.b : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], IsPGroup 2 G → IsBinaryFinite G →
      (Infinite G ∨ 2 < Nat.card G) → ¬ IsSimpleGroup G := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«4.74»

items: '2-group' is taken in the sense appropriate for possibly infinite groups: every element has order a power of 2, i.e. Mathlib's `IsPGroup 2 G` (∀ g, ∃ k, g ^ 2 ^ k = 1). No finiteness is imposed on G.

'Order greater than 2' is encoded as `Infinite G ∨ 2 < Nat.card G`, exactly as prescribed by the decomposition table, because `Nat.card G = 0` for infinite G; an equivalent alternative would be `2 < ENat.card G`.

'Binary finite' is formalized as: for all x y, the subgroup `Subgroup.closure {x, y}` is finite (as a type). This matches Shunkov's standard definition ('any two elements generate a finite subgroup'); note that x = y is allowed, which is harmless since a 2-generated subgroup includes 1-generated ones.

The bespoke definition is placed in the problem file (like the definitions in Kourovka/1_40.lean) rather than FormalConjecturesForMathlib, because the task confines all work to the candidate file; a reviewer may prefer to move it to FormalConjecturesForMathlib as a reusable definition.
The group is quantified over `Type` (universe 0), following the convention of the existing Kourovka files.

reviewer_notes: No disagreement among candidates on the mathematics; differences were purely stylistic (inline vs named definition, test vs API category). Verified in Mathlib: IsPGroup p G := ∀ g, ∃ k, g ^ p ^ k = 1 (no finiteness), IsSimpleGroup extends Nontrivial, Nat.card is 0 on infinite types. `2 < ENat.card G` would be an equivalent alternative encoding of the order hypothesis; the decomposition table's disjunction was kept. IsBinaryFinite is generic enough to live in FormalConjecturesForMathlib eventually, but since only a single problem file may be produced it is kept in the problem file (as Kourovka/1_40.lean does with IsEngelGroup). The notebook only lists part b) of 4.74 (part a) was presumably removed as solved), so the slot keeps its letter.
